scene: Your friend posts a story with a tiny hidden text in font size 4 saying 'having a really hard time today'.

q1.prompt: Why did they hide the text so small instead of posting normally?
options: They want to be heard, but feel terrified of being a burden or looking overly dramatic
It was just a typography mistake
They are testing your eyesight

q2.prompt: What is the kindest, lowest-pressure DM to send them?
options: Screenshot it and post it on your story tagging everyone
Send a gentle private DM: 'Saw your story. No need to reply, just sending love and here if you want to vent ❤️'
Reply with a laughing crying emoji

explain: Micro-cries for help on social media come from feeling vulnerable; a quiet private check-in gives comfort without pressure.

scene: You see your entire friend group hanging out on BeReal/Instagram stories without you.

q1.prompt: What is the natural initial emotional sting?
options: FOMO (Fear of Missing Out), feeling excluded and wondering if they dislike you
Pure euphoria
Complete indifference

q2.prompt: What is the most emotionally mature way to handle it?
options: Post passive-aggressive TikToks about fake friends
Breathe, remember plans happen spontaneously, and calmly ask one close friend about it later without hostility
Block everyone in the group immediately

explain: Most exclusions are accidental logistics rather than malice; calm communication prevents unnecessary friendship breakups.

scene: A classmate's private cringey old middle school video is leaked in a large school group chat.

q1.prompt: How does the person in the video feel?
options: Humiliated, betrayed, and terrified of walking into school tomorrow
Excited to go viral
Unbothered

q2.prompt: What is the high-empathy group chat move?
options: Forward it to 10 more chats
Change the subject, say 'Bro we were all cringe in middle school, delete this,' and DM them support
Make memes out of their face

explain: Shutting down public humiliation in group chats protects mental health and shows real backbone.

scene: Popular Gen-Z slang words like 'slay', 'periodt', 'no cap', and 'tea' were invented on TikTok in 2020.

options: Real
Reel

explain: REEL! These terms originated decades ago in African American Vernacular English (AAVE) and Black queer ballroom culture before being popularized on mainstream social apps.

scene: Social media algorithms are designed to maximize outrage and emotional reactions because anger drives higher watch times than calm content.

options: Real
Reel

explain: REAL! Studies show high-arousal negative emotions (anger, shock) generate significantly higher algorithmic engagement and comment traffic.

scene: A 'dopamine detox' where you avoid all fun completely resets your brain's dopamine production to zero.

options: Real
Reel

explain: REEL! Dopamine is a vital neurotransmitter your brain constantly needs to function. 'Detoxing' breaks habit loops and reduces overstimulation, but dopamine is never depleted to zero.

scene: Your friend asks you to define 'Unspoken Rizz'.

q2.prompt: What is the most accurate definition of 'Unspoken Rizz'?
options: Having natural charm and charisma purely through posture, eye contact, and confidence without saying a word
Talking continuously for 20 minutes
Sending 50 memes in a row

explain: 'Rizz' (short for charisma) when unspoken refers to effortless body language and quiet self-assurance.

scene: You open a message from a friend, get distracted, and leave them on 'Read' for 6 hours.

q2.prompt: What is the smoothest way to reply when you remember?
options: “So sorry, opened this while rushing and got sidetracked! Responding now:”
Pretend your phone fell into the ocean
Leave it forever and start a new conversation next month

explain: Honest, quick communication clears up anxiety and prevents misunderstandings.
